data.narrative:
Telexistence, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jin Tomioka and Ken Tomoyose, has raised $170M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) and 1 public comparable, spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $170M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $323M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—produces a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods exhibit substantial divergence, reflecting tension between capital-progression mechanics and peer trading multiples. The triangulated analysis supports a wide range from $275M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.0B. Key uncertainties include revenue run-rate and path to profitability relative to peers, the representativeness of the three-company peer set for a specialized manufacturing robotics player, and whether the $170M raised proxy accurately reflects fair value at entry. Resolution of these factors—particularly revenue scale and unit economics relative to Bedrock and Dexterity—will be material to narrowing the valuation range.
